node.title: Fun with Prototypes
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Can you tell me:

  1. How does this get parsed? (e.g. try adding parentheses to show precedence)
  2. Given that the body of each of the four subs is { print Dumper(\@_) }, what is the output?
$_ = "#x"; my @a = qw/b c/; foo /#(\w+)/, @a; bar /#(\w+)/, @a; quz /#(\w+)/, @a; baz /#(\w+)/, @a;

Hint:

Okay, it's a trick question, I'm trying to make a point about [doc://perlsub#Prototypes] - I didn't give enough information for you to answer it, and if you were already thinking of an answer, sorry but you're probably wrong. So here's the missing information:

sub foo { print Dumper(\@_) } sub bar () { print Dumper(\@_) } sub quz ($) { print Dumper(\@_) } sub baz ($\@) { print Dumper(\@_) }

Solution:

1. Parsing according to perl -MO=Deparse,-p (with some edits for clarity):

foo( /#(\w+)/, @a ); ( bar() / # division; "#(\w+)/, @a;" is a comment quz( /#(\w+)/ ) ), @a; # void context &baz( scalar(/#(\w+)/), \@a );

2. Output (again slightly edited, and without [doc://warnings]):

$VAR1 = ['x','b','c']; # sub foo $VAR1 = []; # sub bar () $VAR1 = [1]; # sub quz ($) $VAR1 = [1, ['b','c']]; # sub baz ($\@)

See [id://861966]. The code was inspired by [merlyn]'s great node [id://44722].
